node.label: Maurice Halbwachs
node.date_label: La théorie de l’homme moyen (1912) · Les cadres sociaux de la mémoire (1925) · La mémoire collective: posthumous publication (1950) · On Collective Memory: edited and translated selections (1992)
node.description: Studies remembering through social frameworks and the changing relations among groups. The selected French conclusion describes how families and religious communities revise their past as they encounter other groups and new present conditions; memory is neither an isolated mental archive nor a perfectly static inheritance. A separate statistical intervention examines the abstraction of an average human being. Canguilhem’s later discussion explicitly takes up that statistical criticism, a particular reception distinct from the collective-memory books. The English On Collective Memory is an edited and translated selection from earlier work, not the beginning of Halbwachs’s inquiry.

proposed_edges.relationship: Reconstructs remembering through social frameworks that change as families, religions and other groups encounter present conditions.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Retained primary conclusion reading digital pp. 205–211, final subsection begins 206, based on 1952 reedition. Newly inspected passage on digital 208–209 corroborates the family/religion examples; electronic pagination is not original 1925 pagination. Generalizations remain the author’s interpretations.

proposed_edges.relationship: Supplies Canguilhem with a specifically acknowledged statistical criticism of the abstract average human being.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Named Canguilhem reception from retained Norme et moyenne selection and bibliography item 53. Halbwachs’s 1912 original remains unread.
